assessment: Alpha.624 fixes a genuine remote avatar LocalID lease ownership bug: a new Full/Compressed simulator Avatar ObjectUpdate using a reused LocalID previously created a second visible remote body while the old UUID and its attached root/child mesh prims stayed alive if prior UDP KillObject was lost. Current connected, nonzero-LocalID real Avatar ObjectUpdate now retires conflicting old avatar UUID, pending animation and linked attachment prim subtree without fabricating an actual KillObject count. When the SAME avatar UUID rebinds to a new LocalID, its authentic prior appearance TextureEntry, VisualParams and attachment metadata stay intact, but its obsolete LocalID-rooted prim meshes are retired pending new server evidence. Identical ObjectUpdates idempotent. Zero LocalID and disconnected ObjectUpdate cannot authorize render body. Native tests exercise crossed UUIDs, old/new LocalIDs, preserved Low158 data, Coarse-only reappearance, independent avatars, KillObject counters and region reset; original Firestorm joint animation GPU framebuffer sees zero stale pixels following current UUID-rebinding. F7 displays separate authenticated current-region rebinding counter. Fresh authenticated NexVerse own skin, COF/outfit and simulator-confirmed WASD end-to-end still open, weighted 38.65% (rounded 39%).
